disagreements.positions: P(>=987): agent_1 0.479, agent_2 0.489, agent_4 0.505, agent_3 0.515, agent_5 0.557. Fair values $950 / $960 / $963 / $983 / $1,015 (mean $974). agent_5 leans above guidance (2028E EPS ~$32.5, EBITDA $11.8B, FCF $9.0B) because guidance has been raised repeatedly.
disagreements.resolution: The Laguna transcript (2026-09-16) says the bigger 2026 change in margin in backlog shows up 'in 29 and 30, because that's most of when that equipment delivers'. 2027-28 deliveries therefore carry older pricing, so the step-up is not a reason to put 2028 EPS above the $56B x 20% outlook (~$30-31 EPS). agent_3 read this correctly. agent_5's second support, a supposedly low Q3 revenue consensus of ~$10.8B, is stale: the current consensus is ~$12.0B, which fits the guide-implied 2H of $25.1-26.1B (1H was $20.44B). Rebuilt on ~$30.5 NTM EPS and ~$8.5B FCF, agent_5's blend is ~$990. Reconciled fair value is ~$970. I take about 1 point off the centre (P(>=987) 0.509 to 0.499).

disagreements.topic: Rate backdrop: fed funds framing vs the long end
disagreements.positions: All five now include the 9/16 hike to 3.75-4.00%. agent_1 alone uses the 10-year (5.29%). agents 3, 4 and 5 lean on prediction-market odds that differ (60%, 77% and 74% hold) to temper the cut to their multiples.
disagreements.resolution: Verified on H.15 (release 2026-10-01): the 10-year rose from 5.18% to 5.29% between 9/24 and 9/30, the 30-year is at 5.64%, the 10-year TIPS yield is 2.93% and the 3-month bill is 4.03-4.20%. The prediction-market figures are not in conflict; they are snapshots from different days. Polymarket October hike odds went from ~67% to ~37% to 23% (hold 77%) on 10/1 after Vice Chair Jefferson signalled patience. A softer October path does not lower long real yields near 3%, and those yields drive what a ~40x 2027E multiple can hold. This supports agent_1's 1x trim and argues against relaxing multiples because October odds fell (agent_4).
disagreements.evidence: Federal Reserve H.15, 2026-10-01; crypto.news / coinspectator, 2026-10-01 (Polymarket 23%); cryptobriefing (37%); financefeeds (67%).

disagreements.topic: 2028 revenue anchor and the hyperscaler capex path
disagreements.positions: agent_2 uses $59B (halfway between the $56B outlook and $61.3B consensus) and cites Goldman's capex growth slowing to ~12% in 2028. agent_1 uses $57B. agents 3 and 4 use $56B. agent_5's EPS sits between outlook and consensus.
disagreements.resolution: Partly settled. The Prolec upside (CEO: 2028 'materially better' than the October-2025 projection) supports $57-58B. Pricing gains on new slots mostly reach revenue and margin after 2028 (Laguna). Goldman's 2027 figure (+~50-54% to ~$1.2T) is well reported. The '12% in 2028' figure circulates mainly through X posts and aggregators with inconsistent totals ($1.4T vs $2T), so it is directionally plausible but unverified as a number. I treat ~$57-58B / ~$30.5 EPS as the anchor. That cuts against agent_5 and slightly against agent_2.
disagreements.evidence: Laguna transcript p.8 (Prolec); Yahoo Finance and TradingView on Goldman's 2027 capex; X/ParadisLabs relay (2028 deceleration).

one_month_reasoning: No edge, so I keep the mean (P(>=987.45) 0.504). 3Q26 results come on 10/28 before the open, the same day as the FOMC decision. Polymarket put an October hike at 23% on 10/1 after Jefferson's remarks, but the 10-year sits at 5.29%. Q3 consensus is ~$12.0B revenue and ~$4.07-4.15 EPS, consistent with the guide, so no beat is set up (agent_5's $10.8B figure is stale). Orders were pre-signalled as strong, but most new slot contracts and the India HVDC order fall in 4Q. The $0.50 dividend record date is 10/27. Oct 31 is a Saturday, so the 10/30 close counts.
confidence_reason: In round 2 the five forecasts converged (P(>=987) 0.48-0.56). My checks settled smaller items: agent_5's above-guidance lean and stale Q3 revenue figure, its thin tails, the 1H buyback price, and the long-end yield level. Together they justify only a ~1-point cut to the centre, which is not enough to replace the mean.
thesis_break_reason: ~$640 (-35%) is ~21x a guidance-anchored ~$30.5 2028E EPS, a no-premium multiple like Siemens Energy's. Four of five agents set $640-650 on the same logic. A sustained close below it would mean slot reservations (63 of 116 GW) failing to convert, the January 2027 margin-in-backlog disclosure stalling, or a real hyperscaler capex cut. Long yields already at 5.3% are in today's price and would not get there alone.
key_drivers: 2028 earnings power is anchored to management's $56B / 20% outlook (~$11.2B EBITDA, ~$30-31 EPS), with Prolec upside. The larger 2026 margin-in-backlog step mostly delivers in 2029-30 (Laguna), so it supports the 2030 outlook at the spring-2027 CMD more than 2028 EPS.

Demand durability: $176B backlog heading past $200B very early in 2027, 116 GW under contract (63 GW reservations), 2032 slots sold with cash down, and 12 GW of new 2030-31 slots at premium pricing, against GLJ's single-source 2030-31 overcapacity case.

FCF normalisation: 2026 FCF of $11.5-12.5B is deposit-driven. The >= $24B 2025-28 floor implies >= ~$8.3B over 2027-28, and the CEO says the progress-payment build is still smaller than the margin added to backlog.
Discount rate: Fed at 3.75-4.00% after the 9/16 hike, 10-year 5.29%, 10-year TIPS 2.93% (H.15, 9/30). A ~40x 2027E multiple is exposed to long real yields more than to the October decision.
Catalyst path: 3Q and FOMC on 10/28, January 2027 call (2027 outlook, margin in backlog, CMD date), spring-2027 CMD with 2030 outlook.

fair_value.reason: Mean of agents' round-2 fair values is $974. summary: In round 2 the five forecasts converged around spot: fair values $950-1,015 (reconciled ~$970), P(>=987) 0.48-0.56. The stock is priced for management's 2028 plan (~$56B revenue, 20% margin, ~$30-31 EPS) at ~32x, with real upside from the spring-2027 CMD's 2030 outlook. The CEO says the 2026 pricing step mostly delivers in 2029-30, so it is not a 2028 EPS driver. Fact-checks trimmed agent_5's above-guidance lean (and its stale Q3 revenue input), corrected the 1H buyback price to ~$848, and confirmed a 5.29% 10-year and 2.9% real yield as the main multiple risk. I take ~1 point off the centre (P(>=987) 0.499), keep the tails and the 1-month ladder at the mean, and keep the thesis break at $640.
